predictions: There is no allele-specific TF binding at this exact site, or any binding difference is not mechanistically connected to obesity.
The GWAS signal is explained by a linked causal variant or by a non-TF-mediated effect, such as a passenger variant in strong LD.
Regulatory assays at this site should not show an allele-dependent effect after controlling for linked variants.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TF ChIP, EMSA, or a regulatory assay shows a reproducible allele-dependent TF binding and enhancer activity that maps to this variant.

chains.title: ARID5B repressor loss at the dELS: risk T loses ARID5B binding and derepresses IRX3/IRX5

links.claim: No QBiC-SELEX model covers ARID5B (E18), and no supplied ChIP, MPRA, or EMSA shows allele-specific ARID5B binding. If ARID5B represses IRX3/IRX5 and T is the GWAS effect/risk allele, the risk T must lose repression relative to alt C, predicting that alt C binds ARID5B more strongly than ref T; this is a hypothesis, not demonstrated by the supplied evidence.
The variant lies in cCRE EH38E3181208, a distal enhancer-like element, so it is in a plausible regulatory element.

IRX3 is 520.4 kb downstream and is a long-range candidate target, but no enhancer-to-IRX3 contact is shown; IRX5 is not listed in E02, and E03 nearby genes do not include IRX3. E19 reports no significant adipose eQTL for this variant, so the gene link is not demonstrated.

Subcutaneous adipose/preadipocyte is the presumed disease-relevant context, but E03 lacks biosample-specific z-scores and E19 found no adipose eQTL, so adipose enhancer activity at this element is not established.

The variant is strongly associated with obesity/BMI and related metabolic traits; the GWAS effect/risk allele is T, which fits a model in which risk T loses ARID5B repression and derepresses IRX3/IRX5 only if the binding direction is as hypothesized.

predictions: Allele-specific ARID5B EMSA or ChIP-qPCR should show stronger ARID5B binding on alt C than ref T.
If ARID5B is a repressor at this element, risk T should permit higher IRX3/IRX5 expression than alt C in preadipocytes.
ARID5B knockdown or motif mutation should reduce or abolish the allele-dependent effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ARID5B EMSA or ChIP-qPCR shows no difference or shows ref T > alt C binding at this site.
Prime editing of ref T to alt C in preadipocytes does not change IRX3 or IRX5 expression.
ARID5B knockdown does not alter the allele-dependent enhancer or gene-expression effect.

chains.title: ESRRA binds the alt allele at the dELS and may alter FTO expression

links.claim: In QBiC-SELEX group G037, ESRRA has its own model and passes with alt-more binding (z 17.39), and the group's best model is also alt-more; this is an in vitro binding prediction only, not allele-specific ChIP or reporter evidence.
The variant lies in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3181208.

FTO is the strongest L2G gene at this locus and the variant is in the FTO gene body; however, FTO is not the nearest protein-coding gene by TSS distance, and E19 reports no significant adipose eQTL, so direct regulation of FTO is not demonstrated.

ESRRA is expressed in subcutaneous adipose in the supplied QBiC context (34.08 TPM), but E20 reports no ENCODE ESRRA ChIP-seq peak containing this variant in adipose; E20 absence can also mean no ESRRA experiment in that biosample, so occupancy is not established.

The variant is strongly associated with obesity/BMI and related metabolic traits. The GWAS effect/risk allele is T, whereas this chain predicts alt C binds ESRRA more; to fit risk T, ESRRA would need to repress FTO or the FTO direction would need to be opposite, and activity direction is not established.

predictions: Allele-specific ESRRA ChIP-qPCR should show stronger ESRRA occupancy on alt C than ref T in adipose or preadipocyte cells.
An allele-specific reporter/MPRA should show an ESRRA-dependent allele effect at this element.
If ESRRA represses FTO, alt C should lower FTO; if ESRRA activates FTO, the direction must be reconciled with T being the GWAS effect/risk allele.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ESRRA ChIP-qPCR shows no alt C > ref T binding difference in adipose or preadipocyte cells.
An allele-specific reporter/MPRA shows no ESRRA-dependent allele effect at this element.
ESRRA knockdown does not change the allele-dependent enhancer or FTO expression effect.

chains.title: NR4A1 binds the alt allele at the dELS and may alter FTO expression

links.claim: In QBiC-SELEX group G002, NR4A1 has its own model and is listed as a passing member with z 16.25; the group's best model is alt-more, but the group contains directionally mixed members and NR4A1's individual sign is not explicitly separated. This is an in vitro binding prediction only.
The variant lies in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3181208.
FTO is the strongest L2G gene at this locus and the variant is in the FTO gene body; E19 reports no significant adipose eQTL, so direct regulation of FTO is not demonstrated.
NR4A1 is highly expressed in subcutaneous adipose in the supplied QBiC context (139.74 TPM), making it a plausible adipocyte TF; no allele-specific NR4A1 ChIP data are supplied.

The variant is strongly associated with obesity/BMI and related metabolic traits. The GWAS effect/risk allele is T, whereas this chain predicts alt C binds NR4A1 more; activity direction is unresolved and would need NR4A1 to repress FTO, or an opposite FTO effect, to fit risk T.

predictions: Allele-specific NR4A1 ChIP-qPCR should show stronger NR4A1 occupancy on alt C than ref T in adipose or preadipocyte cells.
An allele-specific reporter/MPRA should show an NR4A1-dependent allele effect at this element.
NR4A1 knockdown should reduce the allele-dependent enhancer or FTO expression effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific NR4A1 ChIP-qPCR shows no alt C > ref T binding difference in adipose or preadipocyte cells.
An allele-specific reporter/MPRA shows no NR4A1-dependent allele effect at this element.
NR4A1 knockdown does not change the allele-dependent enhancer or FTO expression effect.

grades_v0.reason: No evidence ID is cited for ARID5B binding, no ARID5B QBiC row is shown, and no ChIP/MPRA/allele-specific assay is provided. This is a pure unsupported mechanistic assertion.
E03 places the variant in cCRE EH38E3181208, a dELS, directly supporting the element annotation. The adipose-specific activity is not shown, but the dELS call itself is supported.
E02 only gives IRX3 at 520.4 kb downstream; it does not show enhancer-to-IRX3 contact, and IRX5 is not even listed. The claim is appropriately hedged as a candidate, but the evidence is indirect.
No expression, chromatin, or perturbation evidence is cited for subcutaneous adipose/pre-adipocytes. E03 explicitly lacks biosample-specific z-scores, so adipose enhancer activity is not established.

E04 and E05 directly support strong association of rs1421085 with obesity/BMI and related traits. The adipocyte-enhancer interpretation is not shown by these GWAS/L2G data, but the phenotype association itself is supported.
E08 is QBiC-SELEX in vitro binding only. ESRRA has an own model and passes with alt-more binding z 17.39, but this is a binding prediction, not allele-specific ChIP, MPRA, or reporter evidence.
E03 directly places the variant in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3181208.

E05 supports FTO as the strongest L2G gene (0.99) and E02 places the variant in the FTO gene body. However, the claim that FTO is the nearest protein-coding gene is false: RPGRIP1L is 63.1 kb from TSS while FTO is 65.3 kb.
E08 gives ESRRA expression in the provided adipose subcutaneous context (34.08 TPM), directly supporting expression plausibility. It does not show enhancer activity in adipocytes.

E04 and E05 support strong obesity/BMI association. Direction is not resolved: the GWAS effect/risk allele is T, while the hypothesis proposes alt C binds more and, if ESRRA activates FTO, alt C increases FTO.

E10 is QBiC-SELEX only. NR4A1 is listed as a passing member with z 16.25, but the group has directionally mixed members and NR4A1's individual sign is not explicitly stated. No allele-specific ChIP or perturbation is cited.
E03 directly places the variant in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3181208.

E10 reports NR4A1 at 139.74 TPM in the provided QBiC adipose subcutaneous expression context, directly supporting expression plausibility.
E04 and E05 support strong obesity/BMI association. As with H2, the alt C binding direction is not reconciled with the GWAS risk/effect allele T.

grades_final.reason: E18 only supports ARID5B being not_in_coverage in QBiC-SELEX; it provides no allele-specific ARID5B binding evidence. The claimed alt>C binding direction is explicitly hypothetical.
E03 directly places the variant in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3181208.

Adipose context is plausible, but E03 gives only maxima across biosamples and E19 shows no adipose eQTL, so adipose/preadipocyte enhancer activity is not established.

E08 supports ESRRA expression in subcutaneous adipose, but E20 reports no adipose ENCODE ESRRA ChIP-seq peak containing the variant; E20 also notes absence may reflect missing experiments, so occupancy is not established.

E04/E05 strongly support obesity/BMI association with effect/risk allele T, but the chain predicts alt C binds ESRRA more; reconciling this with risk T requires an unestablished repressive or opposite-FTO direction.
E10 lists NR4A1 as a passing own-model member in G002, but gives no explicit individual NR4A1 effect sign and notes the group has mixed directionality; this is only a QBiC-SELEX binding prediction.

checks.why: H1 has no binding evidence and ARID5B coverage is not shown in any QBiC group row; lookup would establish whether ARID5B has an own/mapped model and what direction, if any, is predicted.
The gene link for H2/H3 currently rests on distance/L2G, not expression QTL in the case context; an adipose eQTL for FTO or IRX3 would strongly change ranking and clarify direction.
ESRRA binding is currently supported only by QBiC-SELEX prediction; an ENCODE/Factorbook peak containing this variant in adipose would test occupancy, though not allele specificity.
